title: Via Separations Internship
text:
Location: Watertown, Massachusetts Duration: June 2024 – September 2024
About Via Separations: Via is a climatetech company tackling the largest source of the US’ industrial emissions and 10-15% of global energy use: industrial separations. Separations are required for the manufacturing of everything we need from paper, food, fuels, to chemicals and more. But today, separations are an expensive and inefficient process that rely on fossil-fueled evaporators.
Via’s technology electrifies this ubiquitous thermal process by using membranes. Unlike other polymer membranes, Via’s technology can withstand all the extremes of the industrial environment due to their use of graphene oxide, a highly-durable and customizable material. Via’s filtration system adds value to their costumers by lowering energy costs and debottlenecking production. Unlike many other climate technologies, Via’s has no “green premium,” meaning Via’s technology is both better for the planet and adds value for the costumer.
My role: At Via, I worked with the Business Operations team, at the intersection of finance, management, and storytelling. My day-to-day responsibilities included: creating fundraise materials (like slide decks), office management, facilities, accounts payable process, and employee hour monthly approvals.
My major projects:

Full website revamp. Successfully proposed a website revamp project for a very out-of-date website. Managed web design contractors and created new materials including a marketing video that I wrote, filmed, and edited.
R&D market and technology research for a potential new application for Via’s technology
Event planning and marketing for the company’s first plant opening event in September

Achievements:

Taking initiative to successfully propose projects.
Working across teams and disciplines
Flexibly adapting to new tasks
Asked to stay on remotely after internship end date to complete video project.

title: Metropolitan Council Internship
text:
Location: St. Paul, Minnesota
Duration: June 2025 – Present

About the Metropolitan Council
The Met Council is a non-elected government agency that provides long-term planning and services for the 7-county Twin Cities Metro Area. The Met Council employs over 4,000 individuals and in 5 divisions, the largest of which is Metro Transit. Metro Transit is the primary public transportation provider for the Twin Cities Metro Area with a network of buses, light rail and commuter trains. In 2024, Metro Transit provided more than 47 million rides across the Twin Cities region! Within this massive organization, I sit on a 6 person team: the Sustainability team. The sustainability team works across the entire Council to conduct climate action planning and implementation, emissions tracking and reporting, natural systems management, environmental justice work, energy utilities management, energy efficiency work, and much more.


My role
At Metro Transit, I work with the Sustainability team, focusing on Greenhouse Gas data analytics.


My major projects

GHG Calculations + Tracking: The current method for calculating the agency’s GHGs is an outdated spreadsheet with lots of manual labor and errors. I am spearheading a new system to calculate, track and report the agency’s GHG emissions. This system automatically pulls data from our utility software to provide monthly reports.
GHG Dashboard: To communicate Metro Transit’s emissions for internal decision making and external reporting, I am creating an interactive GHG dashboard using PowerBI. This dashboard updates automatically and creates clean GHG reports and visuals.
Facilities Energy Targets Dashboard: I am creating a more specialized interactive dashboard displaying energy use by facility. This tool will help the Sustainability, Engineering, and Facilities teams discover trends in each facility and create nuanced targets to lower energy use.



Achievements

Taking initiative to successfully propose projects.
Independently learning new software: PowerBI, EnergyCAP, B3.
Complex data wrangling, analysis, visualization, and communication.

title: Icelandic Oil Sales Dashboard
text:
Location: Iceland
Duration: May 2025

Study abroad
In Spring 2025, I studied abroad in Iceland with the School for International Training’s Iceland: Climate Change and the Arctic program. I lived in Iceland for one semester to study the country’s unique environment and action on climate change. My time there concluded with a 5-week independent study project where I collaborated with Eimur, an Icelandic organization working towards sustainable resource utilization in Northern Iceland, and the EU LIFE-funded RECET project, aiming to empower European rural municipalities in their energy transition planning.


Iceland’s unique energy portfolio
Iceland aims to significantly and quickly change its energy sources with goals of carbon neutrality by 2040 and being fossil fuel-free by 2050. While Iceland’s electricity already originates from 100% renewable energy, it still relies on oil for land transportation, marine transportation, aviation, and industry. With over 60% of Icelanders living in the capital region, Iceland’s clean energy transition must also consider the remaining population living in smaller municipalities and rural areas. Differences in regional Icelandic oil consumption have yet to be studied, and a gap exists between the state and local governments about climate action.


My project
Given this climate action gap, Eimur hoped to publish newly available oil sales data from 2010-2020 to help address prior uncertainty about regional differences in oil consumption. I designed a dashboard exploring data and support accessible exploration of regional differences in Iceland’s oil consumption. The dashboard’s interactive and accesible design supports use by community members and policy-makers alike. Findings and patterns revealed by the dashboard can help inform equitable energy transition policy in Iceland.

title: Environmental Studies + Statistics Senior Honors Thesis
text:
Location: Macalester College, St. Paul, Minnesota.
Duration: September 2025 - May 2026

Honors Thesis
To continue my exploration of oil sales across Icelandic municipalities, I am conducting a 1-year-long Seniors Honors Thesis. Working across disciplines, I am bridging my Environmental Studies and Data Science skills to explore differences in oil across space and time using Small Area Estimation modeling.


Advisors

Dr. Christie Manning, Environmental Studies
Dr. Taylor Okonek, Statistics



Iceland’s unique energy portfolio
Iceland aims to significantly and quickly change its energy sources with goals of carbon neutrality by 2040 and being fossil fuel-free by 2050. While Iceland’s electricity already originates from 100% renewable energy, it still relies on oil for land transportation, marine transportation, aviation, and industry. With over 60% of Icelanders living in the capital region, Iceland’s clean energy transition must also consider the remaining population living in smaller municipalities and rural areas. Differences in regional Icelandic oil consumption have yet to be studied, and a gap exists between the state and local governments about climate action. This project uses newly available oil sales data from 2010-2020 to help address spatial energy consumption uncertainties and promote effective energy transition policies.


Research question
What factors impact oil consumption across time and space in Iceland?

title: Undergraduate Course Highlights
text:
Overview
At Macalester, I have taken a wide-range of courses across disciplines. I decided to pair my major, Environmental Studies, which is interdisciplinary by nature, with a more skills-focused minor, Data Science. I have also taken courses in Economics, Physics, Biology, Art, History, English, and Spanish, providing me with diverse communications, research, and analytical skills.

title: Undergraduate Course Highlights
text:
Environmental Studies

Psychology and/of Climate Change
Cross-listed with Psychology, this course provided me with a framework to understanding why we humans react (or rather, don’t react) to climate change and what are the psychological determinants of taking action.
Skills:

Motivating effective climate action on small and large scales
Behavioral-change climate policy



Earth’s Climate System
This deep dive climate science course taught me what drives energy through the atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere. Understanding how the status quo of the climate translated into understanding why human burning of fossil fuels results in the climate crisis.
Skills:

Climate science (chemistry, physics, and math) skills to solve challening problem sets
Bridging science and policy in Policy-memo

I went on to precept (TA) this course for two semesters! Helping students work on problem sets and grading labs. I often managed working with 12+ students at a time at office hours.


Climate Change: Science, Economics, and Policy
Cross-listed with Economics, this team-taught course taught me the world of climate economics. From externalities, carbon taxes, to climate models and Integrated Assessment Models, I learned how climate scientists and economists make predictions about the future and impactful policies.
Skills:

Modelling: Integrated Assessment Models
Applying economic tools: externality, discount rate, carbon tax, statistics.
Climate Economics Literature Review
